Only issued invoices can be written off.

## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0005] Refunds above 500.00 need second approver: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0007] Record state transitions via audit.record: Every payment/invoice state transition must emit an `audit.record` event named `<entity>_<action>` (e.g. `payment_authorized`, `payment_captured`) carrying the entity id and amount.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Money operations accept idempotency_key first: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` and check it first, before any state validation: scan `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an entry with the same key and return the original record without reapplying. Pass `idempotency_key` into the `audit.record(...)` call.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Use BillingError with snake_case codes: Raise ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a snake_case code string for domain validation failures, e.g. "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity", "negative_amount"; include a short detail string as the second argument.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0002] Reject bool where int is required: When validating integer inputs, explicitly reject bool via isinstance(x, bool) before the int check, since True/False pass isinstance(x, int).
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0003] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize any incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
